thread:
olivia_cs: Ping - customer (Formly) couldn't finish browser onboarding. Calls from their SPA to /v1/embeddings are failing in Chrome with CORS errors. Server-side tests and cURL from their backend succeed.

olivia_cs: They shared a repro: SPA does a fetch to our embeddings endpoint with an ephemeral token in Authorization header. In the browser console they see: 
`Access to fetch at \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings\" from origin \"https://app.formly.co\" has been blocked by CORS policy: Response to preflight request doesn't pass access control check: No \"Access-Control-Allow-Origin\" header.`

olivia_cs: When they inspect network trace the OPTIONS preflight returns HTTP/401 with JSON `{"error":"missing_auth","message":"auth required"}` and no CORS headers. Actual POST request never reaches our service because browser blocks it.

tom_eng: ah — OPTIONS should be allowed unauthenticated and respond with the right CORS headers. Sounds like their proxy or our edge is enforcing auth on OPTIONS and dropping CORS headers on auth failures. Ask them to capture the raw response headers for the OPTIONS.

olivia_cs: they provided headers for the OPTIONS (from browser devtools):
- status: 401
- content-type: application/json
- x-request-id: req_c0f1
(no Access-Control-Allow-* headers present)

sana_frontend: confirm if their SPA sends Authorization on the preflight? Browsers don't send credentials on preflight by default. Preflight is unauthenticated; servers must answer it without requiring auth.

tom_eng: exactly. Two remediation paths: 1) server/proxy rule change: allow unauthenticated OPTIONS and always respond with Access-Control-Allow-Origin and other CORS headers; 2) temporary workaround: host a tiny proxy on their backend that adds CORS headers (not ideal long-term). For onboarding, recommend option (1).

infra-bot: note logged: infra/edge #582 allow unauthenticated OPTIONS for CORS preflight -> triage.

olivia_cs: customer says their internal Nginx had a rule requiring auth for all paths; they can patch it to `if ($request_method = OPTIONS) { return 204; }` with proper CORS headers. They asked for exact header set to return.

tom_eng: give them this minimal response for preflight:
- status: 204
- Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://app.formly.co (or *)
- Access-Control-Allow-Methods: POST, OPTIONS
- Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization, Content-Type
- Access-Control-Max-Age: 3600
That will let the browser proceed to the POST which will include Authorization.

sana_frontend: add a note: browser preflight never includes the Authorization header, so requiring auth on OPTIONS always fails. Also recommend keeping Access-Control-Allow-Headers to include Authorization so the subsequent request is allowed.

infra-bot: infra ticket updated with headers snippet and repro request-id req_c0f1.

olivia_cs: customer applied the Nginx patch and the SPA tests passed. They also found that their auth middleware had a strict 401 response without CORS headers; patch fixed it.

tom_eng: follow-ups: 1) ask CS to add a short KB entry in onboarding: "If you run CORS-protected SPAs, ensure proxy/edge allows unauthenticated OPTIONS and returns CORS headers (include Authorization in Access-Control-Allow-Headers)." 2) SDK note: browser SDK quickstart should call out server-side CORS expectations for ephemeral token flows.

olivia_cs: noted. I'll mark renewal-risk as low and schedule a 20-min enablement call to review prod CORS settings. I'll attach repro and the infra ticket to the support case and close when KB lands.

sana_frontend: also reminded the customer to avoid sending tokens in query params; browser devtools will log them and some CDNs strip query auth.

olivia_cs: thanks all — closing loop with customer now. :white_check_mark:
